## Which tours pass through the Valley of Rocks near Alota?

The [Valley of Rocks near Alota](/bolivia/place/valley-of-rocks-alota/) lies in southwestern Bolivia, along the high-altitude roads of Sud Lípez. Massive, unusually shaped rock formations rise from the open desert landscape. Their outlines were shaped by wind, temperature fluctuations and other weathering processes. For travelers, the valley offers an opportunity to pause among these stone formations while traveling between more remote natural landmarks.

**Your choice of tour should primarily depend on what comes before and after Alota.** The rocky valley occupies only part of a much longer high-altitude route. Some itineraries first visit the Uyuni Salt Flat, then the lagoons and geysers, reaching the valley on the return journey. Others include the rock formations on a separate day's drive through the southern Altiplano before continuing to other natural sights.

This catalog contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that visit the Valley of Rocks as part of the main itinerary.

| Tour | When Alota is visited |
|---|---|
| [Bolivia in 11 days](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) | On the return from the lagoons to Uyuni |
| [Treasures of Bolivia, 12 days](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) | After Siloli, the geysers and Laguna Verde |
| [Peru and Bolivia, 15 days](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) | During the journey through the Valley of Rocks |

In all three journeys, the Valley of Rocks forms part of an extensive itinerary. The stated number of days covers the entire tour, including cities, other natural areas and drives. It tells you nothing about how long the walk among the rocks will last.

## Bolivia in 11 days: from Titicaca to Uyuni and Torotoro

The [“Bolivia in 11 Days: Titicaca, La Paz, Uyuni and Torotoro” tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) connects several of the country's natural zones and cultural regions. Its highland portion begins with [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/) and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/), after which the road continues toward the lagoons and volcanic deserts.

The Valley of Rocks appears on **day seven**, after several other major stops. The route first passes through the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and the [Polques hot springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/). Travelers then head to [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) and, on the return journey toward Uyuni, stop at the large volcanic rocks near Alota. [San Cristóbal](/bolivia/place/san-cristobal/) follows the valley. According to the tour description, the group returns to Uyuni in the evening.

It is a full day: the scenery shifts between stony desert, red and green lagoons, geothermal fields and a valley of boulders. **Alota is therefore the final natural stop on a major highland circuit.** No separate walking time at the site is specified, so it would be misleading to promise several hours exploring the rocks.

The journey then continues to Cochabamba and [Torotoro](/bolivia/place/torotoro/), where the main attractions are caves, canyons and traces of prehistoric animals. This tour suits travelers who want to combine rocky highland scenery with [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/), historical landmarks and the very different natural setting of Torotoro.

## Treasures of Bolivia in 12 days: the rocky valley after the lagoons

On the [12-day Treasures of Bolivia itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/), travelers begin with cities and cultural landmarks. The route passes through [Santa Cruz](/bolivia/place/santa-cruz/), Samaipata, [Sucre](/bolivia/place/sucre/) and [Potosí](/bolivia/place/potosi/). The nature-focused section around Uyuni and the high-altitude lagoons follows.

On the day devoted to the Siloli Desert, the group sets off early in the morning. The itinerary includes the Stone Tree, the red lagoon, the Sol de Mañana geothermal area, Polques, the Dalí Desert and the green lagoon near Licancabur Volcano. **The return journey includes the Valley of Rocks near Alota and San Cristóbal.** The route description places the return to Uyuni in the evening.

At first glance, this section resembles day seven of the previous tour: both itineraries visit the colorful lagoons and finish their highland day by returning toward the salt flat. The overall journeys are different, however. Treasures of Bolivia devotes more attention to historic cities, architecture and cultural heritage, and later reaches Titicaca and [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/).

This is a convenient choice if you want to experience **the Valley of Rocks within a broader journey through Bolivia's history and landscapes**, without adding Peru and a separate international transfer. The presence of accompanying guides and the exact services included should be assessed from the chosen itinerary; arrangements may vary from one day to another.

## Peru and Bolivia in 15 days: Alota on a separate highland crossing

[“Peru and Bolivia: Uyuni and the Altiplano Lakes”](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) differs considerably from the two Bolivia-only tours. Travelers begin with Lima, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Titicaca. The journey then passes through Bolivia's [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) toward the Uyuni Salt Flat.

**Day nine** is devoted to the salt flat itself and the cactus island. **Day ten** focuses on the rocky landscapes of the southern Altiplano. After leaving Colchani, the route passes the [San Cristóbal](/bolivia/place/san-cristobal/) area, the red rocks of the Valley of Rocks and the surroundings of Ollagüe Volcano. High-altitude lagoons follow, with a drive to Ojo de Perdiz. On day eleven, the itinerary includes the [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/), Laguna Colorada, Sol de Mañana, hot springs and Laguna Verde.

The key distinction from the 11- and 12-day journeys is that **the Valley of Rocks comes before the day of geysers and colorful lagoons, not after it**. The route moves gradually through the southern Altiplano with an overnight stop, instead of returning to Uyuni on the same day as the visit to the Valley of Rocks.

Choose this itinerary if you also want to see Inca heritage, Machu Picchu and the islands of Titicaca alongside the high-altitude deserts. Fifteen days allow more regions to be included in one journey, but they also mean more transfers and changes in altitude.

## How the Valley of Rocks differs from other rocky landscapes

Southwestern Bolivia has several natural landmarks known for unusual rock formations. They are easy to confuse, especially when a single day's itinerary mentions a desert, the Stone Tree and the Valley of Rocks.

**The Valley of Rocks near Alota** is a concentration of large rock formations along a highland road. Travelers see them during a stop and a short walk in the open landscape. Their shape, arrangement and texture are the main attractions.

**The Stone Tree** is a separate, well-known rock formation in the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/) area. Its distinctive silhouette makes it an attraction in its own right. A stop at the Stone Tree should not automatically be treated as a visit to the Valley of Rocks near Alota: these are geographically distinct stops.

**[Moon Valley near La Paz](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/)** is in a completely different part of Bolivia. Its narrow, eroded formations and proximity to the city make it suitable for a city excursion day. The valley near Alota belongs to a longer high-altitude journey through the salt flat and lagoons.

The [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) itself is yet another type of landscape. Its immense expanse of salt and mirror-like reflections after rain are very different from the reddish stone formations. A trip that includes both therefore provides considerable variety even within one natural region.

## What else to see on the road through Alota

Most travelers visit the Valley of Rocks alongside other stops in southwestern Bolivia. Depending on the itinerary, the sequence may include:

- [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/) and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/), with salt-flat landscapes and views from the cactus island.
- The [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), featuring arid highlands, volcanic rocks and colored lakes.
- The [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and [Polques hot springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/), where geothermal activity is the main attraction.
- [San Cristóbal](/bolivia/place/san-cristobal/), a settlement on several of the routes toward Uyuni.

These are **stops on the same broader journey**, not attractions within walking distance of the Valley of Rocks. Distances between them on the southern Altiplano can be considerable, while the actual route depends on the condition of unpaved roads. Do not expect to see all of them on a single independent walk.

If nature-focused journeys without Peru are your priority, compare [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/). To see all programs that specifically pass through the salt flat, explore the [selection of tours visiting Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/tour/). This selection concerns a narrower area: the stop near Alota.

## When to visit the Valley of Rocks and how to prepare

The highland roads of southern Bolivia cross open terrain where strong sunshine comes with cold winds and sharp changes in temperature. For a short walk over stony ground, wear closed shoes with dependable soles and bring sunglasses, a hat and warm clothing. It is best to have drinking water ready before leaving a settlement.

The season affects both the experience and travel conditions. During rainy months, some routes near the salt flat and on unpaved stretches can change because of water and road conditions. In dry weather the surface and access roads are generally more stable, although some sections remain challenging. The exact sequence of natural stops depends on conditions during the journey.

Altitude is another factor on the southern Altiplano. Some travelers feel unwell after a rapid ascent, developing headaches, weakness or breathlessness. If your condition deteriorates noticeably, do not continue gaining altitude as though nothing is wrong; inform those accompanying you and seek medical assistance when necessary. Anyone with a medical condition affecting altitude tolerance should discuss their itinerary with a doctor in advance.

**Do not assume a lengthy hiking excursion merely because an itinerary mentions the “Valley of Rocks.”** On the confirmed tours, the stop falls within busy highland days, with much of the time spent driving and visiting several distant places. For the exact duration of the stop and any possibility of changing the order, refer to the terms of the specific itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through the Valley of Rocks

### Where is the Valley of Rocks near Alota?

In southwestern Bolivia, along the high-altitude roads near Alota and Sud Lípez. It features on routes between the Uyuni Salt Flat and the natural landmarks of the southern Altiplano. The [place's own page](/bolivia/place/valley-of-rocks-alota/) describes the valley itself, while this catalog covers journeys passing through it.

### Can the Valley of Rocks and Laguna Verde be visited together?

Yes. On the [11-day Bolivia tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) and [Treasures of Bolivia](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/), Alota is visited on the return journey after [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/). On the [15-day Peru and Bolivia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/), the rocky valley is scheduled one day before Laguna Verde.

### What is the difference between the 11-day and 12-day tours?

Both visit Alota after the high-altitude lagoons, but their overall geography differs. The [11-day tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) also includes the caves and canyons of Torotoro. The [12-day tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) devotes a substantial portion to Bolivia's historic cities, including Sucre and Potosí.

### Which tour should you choose if you also want Machu Picchu and Titicaca?

The [15-day “Peru and Bolivia: Uyuni and the Altiplano Lakes” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/). It combines [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), the islands of Titicaca, Uyuni, the Valley of Rocks, lagoons and geothermal areas.

### Are you guaranteed to be able to walk among the formations?

The tours describe the Valley of Rocks as a sightseeing stop. The precise walking time, access to individual rocks and availability of particular areas depend on weather, roads and the itinerary's arrangements. If a substantial hike is important to you, it should be agreed separately rather than inferred from the place name alone.

### Can the Valley of Rocks be visited without a multi-day trip?

A separate overland itinerary in southwestern Bolivia could theoretically be arranged, but this catalog contains only Ada Tours' published journeys where Alota forms part of a multi-day program. No standalone one-day product is advertised here.

## Excursions to the Polques hot springs in Bolivia

The [Polques hot springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/) are situated on the high-altitude Altiplano of southern Bolivia, along natural routes through the Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna Reserve. Warm water contrasts with cold, open plateaus, volcanic slopes and colorful lagoons. Most travelers reach the springs during longer road journeys through the southwest of the country.

**Polques is a stop within a route, not a standalone urban spa complex.** The main appeal is the combination of the thermal area and its natural surroundings. Whether bathing is possible, how long the stop lasts, whether facilities are operating and the access conditions depend on the itinerary and the circumstances on the day.

## Which Ada Tours excursions visit Polques?

The Polques springs are included in two of our excursion routes. Their shared geography does not make the programs identical.

### Across the Altiplano toward the Chilean border

[“Across the Bolivian Altiplano to San Pedro de Atacama”](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-altiplano-border-transfer/) is an off-road vehicle journey with natural stops in Bolivia, followed by a border crossing into Chile. The route includes [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), Polques, [Laguna Blanca](/bolivia/place/laguna-blanca/) and [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/).

This format suits travelers for whom discovering the high-altitude landscapes is also part of the transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The journey lasts approximately 8–9 hours. When choosing it, separately confirm border-crossing documents and timing, onward accommodation and transport arrangements on the Chilean side.

### Eduardo Avaroa lagoons, returning to Uyuni

[“Eduardo Avaroa: Red and Green Lagoons”](/bolivia/ojo-de-perdiz/eduardo-avaroa-colorada-verde-uyuni/) is a full-day journey from Ojo de Perdiz via the [Stone Tree](/bolivia/place/arbol-de-piedra/), [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/), Laguna Colorada and geothermal areas to Laguna Verde. The route visits Polques and, after the natural stops, includes a transfer to Uyuni Airport.

Here, **crossing into Chile is not part of the program**. Although both excursions visit Polques, their direction of travel and end-of-day logistics differ. That distinction matters for travelers continuing within Bolivia or departing from Uyuni.

## Polques on an Altiplano itinerary: what else to see

The springs are rarely the sole reason to undertake a long journey through the southern Altiplano. The surroundings contain sharply contrasting scenery: the reddish water of Laguna Colorada, steam and hot ground at Sol de Mañana, and the mineral shades of lakes Blanca and Verde. All these natural sites are exposed to dry high-altitude conditions.

To appreciate the region, it helps to distinguish three experiences: thermal water at Polques; geothermal phenomena involving steam and hot ground at [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/); and colorful mountain lakes. Polques is not the same as a geyser field, even if both are visited on the same day.

Bolivia's official protected-areas portal describes the Eduardo Avaroa Reserve as a destination known for multicolored lagoons, geothermal features, desert landscapes and Andean birds. The environment requires care: driving off permitted roads, approaching hot ground and stopping outside designated areas can be dangerous.

## Can you bathe at Polques?

Thermal bathing pools are known at the site, but **a stop at the springs on an excursion does not in itself confirm that bathing is an included service**. The length of the stop, current access, time to change clothes and conditions for the particular group all matter.

If bathing is an essential goal of your journey, discuss it with the organizer in advance. Otherwise, it is more sensible to see Polques as a natural stop where there may be an opportunity to relax if conditions allow.

Even when a pool is available, keep in mind the substantial contrast between water and air temperatures. At high altitude, people respond differently to sustained physical activity and sudden weather changes; those with medical limitations should discuss both the journey and bathing with a doctor beforehand.

## Preparing for a high-altitude road journey

You will travel through areas where settlements are far apart and weather can change quickly. Pack layers, a warm jacket, sun protection, drinking water and comfortable closed footwear. Separate bathing items may be needed if your itinerary permits swimming.

Avoid scheduling too tightly on a day when you enter Chile or fly out of Uyuni. Even if the excursion's stated duration is known, roads, border formalities and natural stops introduce uncertainty. For a cross-border itinerary, check the entry requirements applicable to your nationality and route.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions to Polques

### Can Polques be visited on a trip from Uyuni?

Yes. Both our excursion routes pass through Polques, but their endpoints differ: one heads toward the Chilean border and the other returns to Uyuni.

### Is bathing possible on every excursion?

There is no confirmation that bathing is included in both programs. Both visit the springs, but the opportunity to swim and the time allocated must be checked separately.

### Which option should you choose if Chile comes next?

The [Altiplano route to San Pedro de Atacama](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-altiplano-border-transfer/) is suitable. It includes the drive to the border and continuation into Chile. A separate lagoon route is available for those staying in Bolivia.

### Are Sol de Mañana and Polques the same place?

No. [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) is a geothermal field with steam and hot ground, while [Polques](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/) is a hot-springs site. Both may feature in one excursion day.

### Is acclimatization necessary?

High-altitude itineraries require attention to individual altitude tolerance. If arriving from a low elevation, discuss the pace of ascent and time to acclimatize before starting a long day on the road; anyone with relevant health conditions should seek individual medical advice.

## Excursions in Potosí: the history of silver and a visit to the Cerro Rico mines

[Potosí](/bolivia/place/potosi/) is a high-altitude Bolivian city that developed at the foot of Cerro Rico, a mountain famous for centuries of silver mining. The city's history is reflected in its architecture, religious buildings and old industrial structures. One of its most memorable excursion themes, however, is the opportunity to learn about miners' work in active underground workings.

**We offer a four-hour excursion to the miners' market and Cerro Rico mines.** It focuses on a living mining culture and therefore differs from a conventional walking tour through the historic center.

## What the Ada Tours itinerary includes

The [“Four-Hour Potosí City Excursion”](/bolivia/potosi/potosi-city-tour/) includes an English-speaking guide and transfers. The itinerary lists several stages in sequence.

1. **Miners' market.** Learn about the items miners use at work and local customs. The guide explains the importance of coca leaves and other aspects of everyday mining life.
2. **Cerro Rico.** Travel to the mountain around which Potosí's silver-mining history developed.
3. **Mine visit.** Descend into underground workings, view tunnels and learn about traditional extraction methods, working conditions and rituals.
4. **Return to the city.** The excursion concludes after the underground portion.

The excursion starts with a morning hotel departure, at approximately 09:00. English-speaking guiding and transfers are included. **Lunch is not included.** The specific access conditions at the mines, equipment, permissible depth of the route and current visiting arrangements must be confirmed for the chosen date.

## Why the Potosí mines matter historically

According to UNESCO, in the sixteenth century Potosí was one of the world's largest centers of industrial silver extraction. The city's heritage includes Cerro Rico, water-supply systems serving industrial facilities, old smelting and processing sites, the Royal Mint and colonial buildings.

The city's inclusion on the UNESCO World Heritage List is not simply about beautiful facades. It preserves evidence of an entire production chain, from extracting ore to making silver ingots and coins. The history of that wealth also involves the harsh and forced labor of Indigenous people, so an excursion about mining culture calls for respect toward those who live and work here.

The [city of Potosí](/bolivia/place/potosi/) deserves a separate walk through its historic neighborhoods. Our excursion, with its underground portion, addresses a more specific subject: seeing conditions in working mines and hearing about local traditions.

## A mining excursion or a city tour?

| Option | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Cerro Rico mines | Miners' work and tunnels |
| Historic center | Architecture, squares and museums |

If silver-boom architecture, museums and city streets are your primary interests, allow time for a separate historical walking itinerary. The [four-hour Ada Tours excursion](/bolivia/potosi/potosi-city-tour/) focuses on the miners' market and mines; visiting every city landmark described on the Potosí page is not part of this program.

For a first visit, the two themes complement one another. The underground portion helps explain the origins of the colonial city's wealth, while the architecture shows how that wealth shaped its development.

## Altitude and safety: what to discuss in advance

Potosí stands at approximately 4,000 m above sea level. Even an ordinary walk can feel more strenuous for someone who has recently arrived from a lowland area. The underground route introduces additional conditions: narrow passages, uneven ground, limited visibility and potential ventilation issues.

Before booking, clarify:

- whether children and people with medical limitations are permitted in the selected section;
- whether a helmet, lighting and other necessary protective equipment are provided and included in the price;
- which restrictions apply to people with claustrophobia or respiratory and cardiovascular conditions;
- where and under what circumstances you can choose not to enter the underground portion.

UNESCO has documented long-term stability concerns in parts of Cerro Rico caused by mine workings. Visits must therefore be restricted to areas permitted by responsible guides and current safety rules; entering adits without authorization is unacceptable.

This excursion is not suitable for everyone. If you have doubts about your well-being, choosing a city itinerary without a descent in advance is better than trying to overcome restrictions on site.

## Understanding prices and conditions

The [Potosí excursion](/bolivia/potosi/potosi-city-tour/) has different rates according to the number of participants. The cost for one person differs from the per-person rate for groups of two or three. Before choosing, compare the rate for your group size, the included transfers and guide language, and the exclusions; lunch is paid for separately.

The excursion lasts about four hours, but it should not be scheduled immediately before an intercity journey or flight without allowing sufficient time. Leave a margin for the return, rest and adjustment to altitude.

## Frequently asked questions about the Potosí excursion

### Does the excursion include a visit to a real mine?

Yes. Ada Tours' current description explicitly includes entering working mines on Cerro Rico and learning about miners' work. Access arrangements and the safe sections are confirmed for the chosen date.

### What language is the excursion conducted in?

An **English-speaking guide** is specified. Russian-language guiding is not advertised as an included service.

### How long does the excursion take?

Approximately **4 hours**. It includes transfers, the miners' market, an underground visit and the return to the city.

### Are meals and protective equipment included?

Lunch is explicitly **not included**. Protective equipment is not detailed in the listing and should therefore be checked separately before visiting the mines.

### Can the underground portion be replaced with a city walk?

The published product focuses on the mines. A different city itinerary must be agreed separately; it should not be assumed to be a substitution already included in the stated four-hour program.

## Potosí and the Cerro Rico mines: an excursion into the history of silver mining

[Potosí](/bolivia/place/potosi/) developed around the rich deposits of silver ore in Cerro Rico mountain. During the sixteenth century, the area became one of the largest industrial centers of its time. Today, the history of the mines can be seen in the city's buildings and the lives of its miners. Historic Potosí and the industrial heritage of Cerro Rico are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

**Our excursion lasts 4 hours.** Its defining feature is an introduction to living mining culture through a visit to the miners' market and a descent into the mines, rather than simply viewing colonial facades.

## What happens at the miners' market and underground

The program begins **at 09:00 with departure from the hotel**. After the transfer, guests visit the miners' market, where the guide explains mining customs, tools and working materials. Coca leaves feature prominently in this explanation, as do traditions associated with Tío, a figure in miners' beliefs to whom offerings are made and protection is requested.

The route then continues to **Cerro Rico**. Guests descend into a mine, learn about the layout of its tunnels and observe miners' working conditions. This part of the excursion makes the connection between silver extraction, the development of the colonial city and contemporary life in Potosí clearer.

A mine visit is a serious encounter with miners' work. Treat working people respectfully, follow the accompanying guide's instructions, stay with the group and do not interfere with industrial operations. Arrange photography of people and working areas with the guide.

## Altitude and safety: who is this excursion suitable for?

Potosí is high in the Andes, approximately **4,000 m above sea level**. Even a normal city walk may require adjustment to the altitude. Going underground adds narrow passages, darkness, uneven surfaces and industrial hazards.

This excursion is suited to visitors prepared for an underground visit and physical discomfort. Those with respiratory or cardiovascular conditions, who are pregnant, have a pronounced fear of confined spaces or feel unwell at altitude should discuss participation with a doctor and the organizer in advance. **Special equipment and entry requirements are not yet specified in our program**; the actual arrangements should be confirmed for the particular visit.

If your main interest is the architecture and history of the region without entering mines, consider a separate city itinerary rather than treating the mining excursion as an ordinary sightseeing walk.

## Included services and rates

Our program includes **transfers and an English-speaking guide**, while **lunch is not included**. The text lists the following amounts:

| Option | Listed price |
|---|---|
| Base price | $84 |
| 2 participants | $55 per person |
| 3 participants | $50 per person |

The basis for calculating the base amount of $84 is not separately specified and should be confirmed when selecting the group. The two- and three-participant rates are explicitly **per person**. The organizer may alter the order of visits while preserving the purpose of the excursion.

For another cultural experience in Bolivia, explore the [Culture and History section](/interests/culture-and-history/), or read about the city's nature and history on the [Potosí page](/bolivia/place/potosi/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Potosí excursion

### How long does the excursion last?

**4 hours.** Hotel departure is scheduled for **09:00**.

### Is lunch included?

No. Our services include transfers and an English-speaking guide; **lunch is excluded**.

### Do visitors need to enter the mine?

Yes. **Descending into a Cerro Rico mine** is part of the main program. If this is undesirable or medically inadvisable, choose another itinerary.

### How much does it cost for two or three people?

For **2 participants, $55 per person**; for **3, $50 per person**. A separate base amount of **$84** is also listed without a detailed explanation of its calculation basis.

### Can the required equipment be confirmed in advance?

Yes. Protective equipment and the specific entry rules should be agreed before departure, as they are not detailed in the public list of included services.

## Excursions to Samaipata: choosing an archaeological day trip

[Samaipata](/bolivia/place/samaipata/) lies in the foothills of the Andes, approximately 120 km from [Santa Cruz](/bolivia/place/santa-cruz/). The main reason to travel here is to visit **El Fuerte de Samaipata**, an archaeological complex inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. It is a historical destination in its own right and should not be confused with an ordinary city walk in Santa Cruz.

For a day trip, the [“Samaipata and El Fuerte from Santa Cruz” excursion](/bolivia/santa-cruz/samaipata-el-fuerte-tour/) lasts **8 hours**. You travel through green foothills to the archaeological site, have lunch in Samaipata and return to Santa Cruz. The format suits those who want to visit the site in one day without needing to spend a night outside the city.

## What you will see at El Fuerte

The name “El Fuerte” is often translated as “the fortress,” but the monument is much more complex than a conventional military fortification. Its central feature is an enormous worked rock surface with depressions, channels, carved figures and evidence of ceremonial use. To the south are remains of residential and administrative buildings.

UNESCO associates the complex with several periods of pre-Hispanic history, including the Mojocoyas culture and the presence of the Incas. On an excursion, it is worth looking not only at the great rock itself but also at the layout of the surrounding structures. A more detailed historical account appears on the [Samaipata destination page](/bolivia/place/samaipata/); here the main focus is how to organize your visit.

Access to the carved rock surface is restricted by heritage-conservation rules. Visitors should stay on permitted paths and follow the guide's instructions. Climbing on ancient surfaces or trying to photograph the site from restricted areas can damage the monument.

## What the Ada Tours excursion includes

The [eight-hour itinerary](/bolivia/santa-cruz/samaipata-el-fuerte-tour/) includes **transfers, an English-speaking guide and lunch**. Additional activities are not covered by the listed price. If you need guiding in a different language, extra stops or more time in the village, arrange these separately.

It is useful to divide the day into three parts: the journey from Santa Cruz, the visit to the archaeological complex, and lunch followed by the return. The experience depends on the time spent at the monument itself: a schedule that is too tight leaves less opportunity to examine the rock carvings and surrounding structures.

## How the trip differs from an excursion to Amboró

Another standalone excursion from Santa Cruz goes to [Amboró National Park and the Cuevas waterfalls](/bolivia/santa-cruz/amboro-national-park-cuevas-waterfalls/). This is a nature-focused route with forest trails. Samaipata, by contrast, is primarily an archaeological excursion. Both are described as eight-hour trips, but they offer completely different experiences and should not be treated as interchangeable.

| Travel goal | Suitable trip |
|---|---|
| Archaeology | Samaipata, El Fuerte |
| Forest and waterfalls | Amboró National Park |

Visiting both destinations is more convenient on separate days or as part of a specially planned itinerary. Their relative proximity on a map does not make them a single ready-made excursion. More destinations are listed in the [Bolivia excursions catalog](/bolivia/excursion/).

## Season and road-trip preparation

Samaipata sits above the plains of Santa Cruz, and the archaeological complex is approximately **1,950 m** above sea level. Cool weather, wind and rain are possible along the route; comfortable footwear, drinking water, sun protection and light waterproof clothing are suitable for visiting this open-air site.

Before departure, confirm access arrangements for the complex, road conditions and the current itinerary for your chosen date. These can change and are not determined by the stated duration of “8 hours” alone.

## Frequently asked questions about Samaipata excursions

### How long is the excursion from Santa Cruz?

Ada Tours' published offer specifies **8 hours**, including the journey to Samaipata, the visit to El Fuerte, lunch and the return.

### Are lunch and the guide included?

Yes. The [“Samaipata and El Fuerte” excursion](/bolivia/santa-cruz/samaipata-el-fuerte-tour/) confirms lunch, transfers and an English-speaking guide.

### Is Samaipata better for nature or history lovers?

Primarily for history and archaeology. For forest trails and waterfalls, compare it with the [Amboró excursion](/bolivia/santa-cruz/amboro-national-park-cuevas-waterfalls/).

### Can Samaipata be visited without staying overnight?

Yes. The published excursion is organized as a day trip from Santa Cruz, returning to the city.
